## Nov 23: saving the spiral stairs work went wrong once, then fixed

**What happened**
- Several chats change the same code files at the same time. Claude saves (commits) only its own changed lines.
- Claude's first save of the spiral-stairs work put some lines in the wrong spot in `dwarf.gd` and `pieces.gd`.
  It also took along two half-finished pieces of another chat's camera/sprint code. The saved copy would not have
  started. The files on the PC were fine the whole time.
- Why: the "only my lines" patch gave positions by line number with no surrounding lines to check against. The
  Twin Gate chat had just saved and undone a change in the same file, so the numbers pointed to the wrong lines.
  The other chat hit the same trap an hour earlier.
- Fix: a fix-up save (9467e2c0). Claude rebuilt both files from the last good saved copy plus only the spiral changes,
  applying them by exact line, bottom to top. Then it checked them against the files on the PC.
- Lesson: after a partial save, always compare the saved file with "old version + my changes" before moving on.


# Dodge "backward then forward" — the real root cause (F702 follow-up)

## What happened
Earlier tonight I fixed a grace-buffer and a dash-speed ramp for the held dodge, called it fixed, and told the
owner to test. The owner came back: "No, still works exactly as before. I'm looking forward, I press Ctrl, I
dash backwards, then I press Ctrl again, I dash forward." Standing still, no movement key held.

## The real bug
`dwarf_fight.gd`'s dodge code had a line that, on purpose, made a standing-still dodge roll **backward**
(`Basis(...) * Vector3.BACK`). But the dwarf's body snaps to face whichever way it just rolled. So: roll 1 goes
backward, body now faces that way; roll 2's "backward" (relative to the new facing) is the opposite of roll 1's
world direction — which looks exactly like "dash backward, then dash forward," over and over.

Nobody ever asked for a backstep-by-default; it wasn't in FEEDBACK.md or FEEDBACK-done.md anywhere. Changed the
fallback to roll the way you're already facing instead.

## My mistake
My first round of automated tests for F702 all held a movement key (W) while testing dodge direction — none of
them tested "stand still, dodge, no keys held at all." That's the exact case the owner was hitting, so my tests
gave false confidence: they passed while the real bug was still there. Added a new test,
`test_dodging_with_no_movement_key_rolls_forward_not_backstep`, that covers exactly that case.

## A side mistake while testing
Checking just my new test file alone with `--check-only --script tests/test_dwarf.gd` failed with a wall of
unrelated "failed to compile depended scripts" errors. Chased it down to `src/player/camera_room.gd` — a new
file from another Claude session, not yet committed. Godot's single-file `--check-only` doesn't do a full
project scan, so it can't see a brand new global class yet; running the real test suite (which does a full
project load) compiled fine. Lesson: a single-file `--check-only` cascade can be a red herring when someone else
just added an uncommitted new script — the full test runner is the real check.

## Still open
The owner's other complaint — "if I press Ctrl and hold, I dodge the same short distance, then basically
sprints the rest of the way" — is NOT fixed yet. The code for a held dash (speed ramps up the longer you hold,
up to Combat.DASH_HOLD_MAX) looks right by reading it, and my simulated test for it passes, but I can't explain
why it would look right in simulation and not match the owner's real-hardware play. Needs real play-testing,
not more code reading, to pin down.

## What's committed
`src/combat/dwarf_fight.gd` (the direction fix) and the new test in `tests/test_dwarf.gd`, as commit
`216f6f66`. Left `src/player/dwarf.gd` and the rest of `tests/test_dwarf.gd` alone — another Claude session has
unrelated, uncommitted camera/sprint work in progress there.

## Nov 23: F807/F798, the jump that finished early and "sprinted" through the air

**What we did**
- The owner reported (after the dodge/dash fix): "the animation should be slowed down when he jumps... the
  animation finishes and then he just sprints forward... we've been working in circles and haven't figured it out."
- First ruled out the easy guesses: there's no separate "long jump" move in the code, and the jump pose isn't a
  looping clip that restarts (it's a short clip that just holds its last frame once it runs out, same idea as a
  paused video). That holding was the actual bug: the jump pose clip is only about half a second long, but a real
  jump can hang in the air well over a second (bigger launch speed = longer hang time, same arc either way). Once
  the clip ran out, the legs froze on its last frame — and if that frame looked anything like a running stride,
  the dwarf looked like he was already running while he was still sailing through the air.
- Fixed it the same way the dodge roll already fixes a similar problem (F702): stretch the clip's playback speed
  to match how long this specific jump is expected to stay in the air, instead of always playing it at the clip's
  own fixed speed. The expected hang time is worked out the moment he leaves the ground, from the jump's launch
  speed and gravity (schoolbook "how long does a thrown ball stay up" math) — a step off a ledge (not a real jump)
  skips this and plays the clip at its normal speed, same as before.
- Changed `src/player/dwarf_rig.gd` (added a speed-control knob to the jump pose in the animation blend tree, same
  pattern as the one already feeding the roll), `src/player/dwarf.gd` (works out the expected hang time when a
  jump starts) and `src/player/dwarf_model.gd` (passes it through). New test:
  `test_jump_animation_is_stretched_to_match_how_long_hes_really_airborne` in `tests/test_dwarf.gd`.
- Logged as F798 (fixed) in FEEDBACK.md.

**Mistakes and hurdles**
- First guess was wrong: suspected the ground-check (`is_on_floor()`) was triggering too early mid-jump and
  cutting the jump short. Reading the animation code ruled this out — the jump pose is a held pose blended by
  amount, not a timed clip that could "finish and loop" on its own, so a ground-detection bug wouldn't explain a
  clip finishing early. The real cause (a too-short clip for a long hang time) only showed up after reading how
  the already-fixed dodge roll solves the exact same kind of problem and checking whether jump had the same fix —
  it didn't.
- `src/player/dwarf.gd`, `tests/test_dwarf.gd` and `FEEDBACK.md` all had another Claude session's unrelated,
  uncommitted work mixed in (sprint/camera code, other feedback items). Committed only this fix's own lines by
  building the commit from a clean copy of each file (read from the last commit, with just this fix's edits
  applied), instead of committing the whole messy working copy.

## Nov 23 — The jump animation fix wasn't actually fixed (F798, F807)

**What we did**
- F798 came back: the owner said "still the same thing... he jumps lands and if it a long jump he just sprints to
  the next stop." The earlier fix (stretch the jump pose to a predicted hang time) only guessed once, at the moment
  he left the ground, assuming he'd land back at the exact same height — true on flat ground, wrong for a real
  running jump across a dip or up onto a rise.
- New fix in `src/player/dwarf.gd`: every physics tick he's airborne, cast a ray straight down to find the real
  ground below him right now, and re-work out how much longer the fall will take from there (`_jump_hang_guess`).
  So the guess keeps catching up to reality instead of being stuck with the first guess.
- Built a new debug robot, `src/debug/jumpcheck.gd`: makes the dwarf sprint and jump, prints the guessed hang time
  every tick next to where he actually is, and takes real screenshots at launch/mid-air/landing so the pose can be
  checked by eye, not just by numbers. Ran it (`jumpcheck claude=... seed=42 shots=...`) and confirmed the live
  guess stayed within about a tenth of a second of the real landing time for the whole flight.
- New test: `test_jump_hang_guess_accounts_for_landing_lower_than_launch` (checks the ray-based guess against a
  real 4 m drop, and that it's longer than the old flat up-and-down guess).

**Hurdles and mistakes**
- First hand-written patch to split my change out of `src/player/dwarf.gd` (see below) failed with
  "corrupt patch" — I miscounted which line a variable actually sat on by hand. Fixed by never hand-counting again:
  pulled the committed version with `git show HEAD:<file> > base.gd`, made a copy, applied my edit to the copy with
  the normal editor, then let `diff -u` work out the line numbers for real.
- Another Claude session had been working in the same two files (`src/player/dwarf.gd`, `tests/test_dwarf.gd`) at
  the same time, on a different, unrelated feature (sprint feel and camera collision, F775/F766), not yet
  committed. Committing those files whole would have swept up their unfinished work under my commit. Used
  `git apply --cached <patch>` to stage only my own hunks into the index, leaving their changes untouched and
  unstaged in the working tree for them to commit separately.
- While isolating my test, found a small pre-existing bug already sitting in the committed code: the test right
  before mine ended with `root.queue_free()` written twice in a row (harmless, just redundant). Fixed it in passing
  since I was already editing that exact spot.
- The debug robot's own first diagnostic print line looked wrong ("expected hang 0.00 s" right at takeoff) — turned
  out to be the print reading the value one tick too early, not a real gameplay bug (it recovered within a tick or
  two, and later runs with a per-tick printout the whole way showed it was never actually wrong). Left as is since
  it's only a debug tool, not something players see.

**Play-test:** a running jump across a real gap — the character should keep moving (legs still mid-air, not
snapped to a running pose) until he actually lands on the far side, however long that jump really takes.

  built pieces inside it; they fade to about half see-through (knob `CAM_BUILD_FADE` in `dwarf_feel.gd`) and fade
  back when they're out of the way. It uses Godot's own per-model "transparency", so every model keeps its paint.

# F805 / F808 / F809 — sprint sticky, double-door, gate bands (Nov 23)

Three feedback items from the Twin Gate play session fixed.

## What we did

### F805 — sprint keeps going after Alt+Tab
**Fix:** `src/main.gd _notification` already released "run" on `NOTIFICATION_APPLICATION_FOCUS_OUT`, but only when the mouse was captured (`Controls.captured()`). If a menu was open (mouse free) and you Alt+Tabbed, the guard was false, so the run key was never released. Added `Input.action_release("run")` and `Input.action_release("dodge")` unconditionally to the FOCUS_OUT branch (the captured-mouse block still runs inside it).

### F808 — pressing E on one gate leaf opens both
**Part A (double door):** Opening a gate_leaf now also opens its partner. Added `_find_gate_partner(uid, p)` to `builder.gd` — it looks for another gate_leaf at the same y, complementary rotation (rot differs by 2), and exactly one leaf-width apart. After `_ev_door.rpc` for the pressed leaf, it fires `_ev_door.rpc(partner, open_to)` with the same value (0 = close, −1/+1 = open direction). Co-op safe: both RPC calls run on the host in `request_door`, which is already authority-only.

**Part B (auto-close after ~30 s):** Exhaustive search through builder.gd, piece_node.gd, game_authority.gd, main.gd, ruin rebuild and load_snapshot — no auto-close timer found. Needs in-game reproduction and further investigation. Marked in FEEDBACK.md but left open.

### F809 — right gate leaf has no iron bands (model fix)
**Root cause:** The gate_leaf model has copper bands on its FRONT face only. The right leaf is the same model rotated 180° (rot=2), so its back faces outward. From outside the gateway you see one leaf with bands and one without.

**Fix:** Added two copper bands to the BACK face in `tools/asset_forge/builds/stonehold_v2.py gate_leaf()`, at y=0.6 and y=1.8 (the batten positions). Used `copper_band(..., z=-0.075, face=-1, rivets=[])`. The z=-0.075 input positions the band's center at z_adj=−0.065 (Godot), which embeds the inner half of the band inside the battens. No rivets on the back (would poke outside the 0.15m box).

**Model rule checks:**
- FLOAT: passed — the band overlaps the batten geometry (BVH overlap = True), so it's "connected"
- OUTLINE: passed — outer face at z=−0.071 is 4mm past the box, under the 5mm OUT_MIN threshold  
- SHIMMER: passed — no coplanar faces (outer face −0.071 vs batten back −0.064 = 7mm apart)
- fit_check: 1mm protrusion warning, but PIECE_OK (warning only)
- All 60 build tests pass

Rebuilt gate_leaf and gate_broken GLBs and re-generated the build menu icons.

## Mistakes and hurdles

- **Back bands float check:** First attempt used z=−0.085 (bands stuck out 6mm and had rivets that poked 1.3cm past the box). Second attempt removed rivets and moved to z=−0.083, still failed FLOAT because the band's sampled corner vertices at x=±0.77 were ~3cm from the batten edge at x=±0.74. Third attempt moved bands to y=0.6/1.8 (batten positions) with z=−0.083, still failed FLOAT — same vertex sampling issue. Final fix: z=−0.075, which places the band center at z_adj=−0.065, overlapping the batten in z so the BVH overlap check fires directly. Four rounds of Blender + check_models before it was clean.

- **Auto-close not found:** Spent significant time searching every plausible location (timers in game_authority, snapshot load, ruin build steps, `_ev_remove_piece`). No auto-close mechanism exists in code. The 30-second timing may be coincidental or caused by a scenario (network sync, menu state) not visible in code alone.

- **Godot not on PATH (Windows):** Had to find the executable via `$LOCALAPPDATA\Microsoft\WinGet\...`. The `.bat` test runner needs `GODOT` set.


## Nov 23 — The held dash's "stand up" animation was finishing mid-burst, not after it (F702)

**What we did**
- F702 came back a 3rd time: "I think I realized the problem. In order for me to do a long dodge, I am holding the
  control key all the way until the dwarf stops rolling... after my animation of the dodge is done, he propels me
  forward." Real self-diagnosis, confirmed exactly right.
- Built a debug robot, `src/debug/dashcheck.gd`: holds the real "dodge" key (Ctrl) like a real keyboard would, prints
  every physics tick's dodge state and roll-animation stretch next to his real position/speed, and takes screenshots
  at key moments.
- Root cause (found from the robot's numbers + screenshots, not guessed): the roll animation clip was always
  stretched to finish in exactly 0.75 s (`Combat.DASH_HOLD_MAX`) for ANY held dash — same stretch a plain quick tap
  gets. A quick tap stops moving well before 0.75 s, so the clip's last bit (stand up, settle) plays while he's
  already stationary — invisible, fine, intended. But a HELD dash keeps speeding up right up to that same 0.75 s
  cap, so that identical "stand up" animation content played out DURING the fastest part of the dash — looking
  exactly like the animation ending and then physics shoving him the rest of the way, which is precisely what the
  owner described.
- Fix: `DwarfFight.dodge_expected_duration()` now returns `DASH_HOLD_MAX + DASH_RECOVERY_TAIL` (0.75 + 0.3 = 1.05 s)
  while a dash is still held, instead of flatly `DASH_HOLD_MAX`. This gives the clip the same kind of "stand up"
  budget a tap roll already gets (the 0.3 s between `DODGE_TIME` and `ROLL_TIME`), but spent AFTER the held dash's
  speed burst ends, during its natural slow-down, instead of during the burst. No changes needed in `dwarf_rig.gd`
  — it already re-stretches the playing clip live to whatever target duration it's given; only the target value was
  wrong. No changes to any tuning numbers (dash distance, speed, hold cap) either — this was purely an animation
  bug.
- Re-ran the same robot after the fix: at t=0.75 s (same distance/speed as the broken run, so a fair comparison),
  he's now still mid-roll instead of already standing; screenshot confirms it (crouched/tucked at t=0.75, back to
  standing only once his velocity has decayed around t=0.95).
- New test `test_held_dash_roll_still_has_recovery_left_when_the_dash_ends`; updated
  `test_roll_animation_matches_how_long_the_dash_lasts` to expect the new, longer stretch.

**Hurdles and mistakes**
- Early on, reasoned abstractly about possible fixes (looping the clip, freezing a frame, etc.) from a summary of
  earlier findings instead of the actual saved robot log and screenshots. Caught it and went back to read the real
  data directly — that's what surfaced the exact, load-bearing detail (`DASH_HOLD_MAX` happens to equal
  `DwarfRig.ROLL_TIME`, both 0.75 s) that explained the whole bug. Lesson: re-read the real evidence, don't reason
  from a paraphrase of it, especially for a timing bug this exact.
- `tools/run_tests.sh`'s `only=` filters by test FILE name, not test function name — `only=dash` matched 0 checks
  (a misleadingly "successful" empty run). `fn=` is the one that filters by function name; the right combo for one
  test file is `only=<file> fn=<function>`.
- `tools/run_tests.sh` needs `GODOT` set on this PC (`godot` isn't on PATH) — same as every other session this week.
- Two already-running Godot processes showed up mid-session; a `taskkill` on them was auto-denied as a destructive
  action. Asked the owner instead of forcing it — they said those were leftovers from testing and fine to close
  (turned out they'd already exited on their own by the time the retry ran).
- Ran the full `test_dwarf.gd` file at the end (not just the dash-filtered subset) and found 3 failures
  (`test_braid_tufts_swing_when_moving`, `test_aim_skips_things_behind_the_dwarf`, `test_your_own_stun_meter`).
  Checked by stashing this session's changes and re-running those 3 on the old code: the hair-swing and stun-meter
  ones fail identically either way (pre-existing, unrelated to this fix); the aim one passed on its own that time
  (flaky dummy-renderer error, not caused by this change). Not touched here.

**Play-test:** hold Ctrl for a long dash — he should still look like he's mid-tumble through the fast part, only
standing up as he slows down near the end, not mid-burst.

- The known bug first: when a piece was removed while see-through, the code put the dead piece into a typed variable
  before checking it, so Godot shouted "previously freed instance" hundreds of times and test_camera_doorway failed.

  same paint, so Godot ran out of room for them ("Too many instances using shader instance variables", ~2000 errors).

  so the "distance from the dwarf on screen" came out negative and counted as the middle everywhere. Fix: `abs()`.

# Dash roll: constant speed, not a speed burst (F702, 4th round)

**What we did:** Last round fixed the roll ANIMATION so it kept playing (tumbling) through a held dash instead of
standing up early. The owner played that fix and liked the animation — but spotted a different, older problem
hiding underneath it: the dwarf's actual travel speed sped up toward the end of a held dash, so he felt "too fast
at the end of the long dodge." The owner's rule was simple: beginning and end of the dash must move at exactly
the same speed. Holding the button should only make the dash last longer, never faster.

**The mistake:** Back in the very first attempt at this feature (Nov 22), we added a `DASH_SPEED_MULT := 1.8`
multiplier that ramped a held dash's speed from 1x up to 1.8x as it approached the 0.75 s hold cap. That was meant
to make "holding it longer" feel like a real forward burst. It's exactly what the owner was complaining about on
the 2nd and 3rd rounds too ("he propels me forward" / "speeds up at the end"), but each time we fixed the
animation-timing SYMPTOM around it instead of asking why he was still speeding up at all.

**The fix:** Deleted `DASH_SPEED_MULT` and the lerp in `DwarfFight.dodge_velocity()` entirely. The dash now always
moves at `DODGE_DISTANCE / DODGE_TIME` (≈6.67 m/s), tap or held, start to finish. Holding the button still makes
the dash travel farther — but only because it keeps moving for longer (up to the same 0.75 s cap as before), never
because it moves faster.

**How we checked it:** Ran the `src/debug/dashcheck.gd` robot (built for the last round's fix) again — it holds
the real dodge key and prints the dwarf's speed every physics tick. Before: speed held at 6.67 for the first
0.45 s, then climbed steadily to ~11.7 by t=0.75 s. After: speed holds flat at 6.67 for the entire 0.75 s hold,
only slowing down naturally once the dash ends and he's standing again. Added a new automated test,
`test_held_dash_moves_at_the_same_speed_start_to_finish`, which samples the dash's speed right after the button
is pressed and right before it ends and checks they match.

**Hurdle:** the full test suite (`tools/run_tests.sh` with no filters) took far longer than its usual ~2-3 minutes
this round — the `GODOT` test process was still visibly chewing through CPU three-quarters of an hour later. Checked
with Windows `Get-Process`: CPU time kept climbing steadily the whole time (not stuck), just starved for CPU
because several other Claude chats were running their own Godot instances on the same PC at once. Ran the
dash-specific tests (`only=test_dwarf fn=dash`) on their own first to confirm the fix quickly, then let the full
suite keep running in the background rather than block on it.

**Also hit:** `test_dwarf_fist.test_great_swings_keep_fists_and_handle_room` failed once, passed the next two times,
with my dash change present both times — confirmed flaky/unrelated (it's about fist-swing handle clearance, not
dodging) rather than a regression, by re-running it a few times.

Files: `src/combat/dwarf_fight.gd` (removed `DASH_SPEED_MULT`, `dodge_velocity()` now constant-speed), minor
comment cleanups in `src/combat/combat.gd` and `tests/test_dwarf.gd` that referenced the old "speeding up" wording,
new test in `tests/test_dwarf.gd`.

## Nov 23: screen-edge effects only showed in the top-left corner (F815)

**What the owner saw:** low health (red edges, blood) and poison/burn/chill looks only covered a box in the top-left of the screen.

**Cause:** the effect layer (`ScreenEdgeFlash`) was told "fill the screen" with `set_anchors_preset`, which sets the anchors but leaves the size at 0. A size-0 box never stretched with the window, so the effect was clipped to a small corner. I measured it: size (0, 0) in a 2000x1100 window.

**Hurdle (mine):** my first low-health test run showed nothing at all, and I could not tell why until I printed the box size. Measuring first saved guessing.

**Fix:** `set_anchors_and_offsets_preset(PRESET_FULL_RECT)`. Now the size is the full window and follows resizing. New test in `tests/test_edge_flash.gd`. The `arenatest lowhp` robot run shows red edges and blood over the whole screen.

## Nov 23: soft lock-on (F790) and the killing-blow pause (F800)

**What we did**
- **F790 soft lock-on:** when a swing starts, `DwarfFight.soft_lock_yaw` looks for living enemies inside a 45° cone
  in front of where the camera looks and within reach (+1 m). It picks the one nearest your aim (closer ones win ties)
  and turns the dwarf toward it, by 25° at most. Enemies beside or behind you are never chosen. The lean stays on for the
  whole swing (`swing_yaw`, used by Dwarf's turning code), so the body doesn't snap back before the hit lands. It only
  runs on the attacker's own game, and the host still decides who gets hit.
- **F800 killing blow:** the host already knew when a hit kills. It now sends that along with the hit (`_ev_hit`'s new
  `killed`). `MonsterManager.hitter_feel` decides what each screen feels: only the killer's screen gets a longer freeze
  (0.15 s, heavy 0.2 s, normal hits 0.06/0.11) and a small camera push-in (`Dwarf.kill_push`, 0.45 m in and back over
  0.45 s, scaled by the camera shake setting, never closer than 1 m). Everyone else plays on as normal. No slow motion.
- All the knobs are in `DwarfFeel` (LOCK_*, KILL_*). 7 new checks in `test_combat` (lock-on never turns toward an enemy
  behind or beside you, ignores far ones, turns at most 25°, picks the aimed-at enemy, works facing any direction;
  only the killer gets the longer pause).

**Hurdles and mistakes**
- `godot` wasn't on this PC's PATH again, so `tools/run_tests.sh` crashed with "file not found". Fixed by setting `GODOT`
  to the WinGet Godot 4.7.2 console exe.
- The full suite showed 295 failures. They came from another chat's cave change (F657, layout 18) that landed while the
  35-minute run was going (`cave_maker.gd:212` out of bounds broke every world-making test). After their commit, the
  world, vitals and combat tests passed again.
- test_dwarf (braid, aim, stun meter, camera rock), test_hud_combat (durability bar) and the bat ragdoll test fail.
  I set my changes aside with `git stash` and ran them again: they fail the same way without my work, so other chats'
  in-progress changes caused them. Left for those chats.
- Only a smoke run in the arena (it starts cleanly, no script errors). The swing itself is for the owner's play test.

## 2026-11-23 (PC) — Carry weight: heavy loads slow you down (F793)
- **Settled with the owner first (grill, 2 rounds + 1 extra):** two-step slowdown (free up to "heavy", then gently

  with no sprint, dodge or jump, still picks things up. Limits go up with the Leather Satchel (+60), the Deep Pockets
  perk, food "carry" buffs, and later backpacks. Mid-chat the owner added stack sizes: now by kind with round numbers
  (stone/ore/wood 50, bars/crystals 30, food 20, drinks 10, ammo 100). Record: `docs/decisions/2026-11-23-carry-weight.md`.
- **Built:** `src/items/item_weights.gd` holds every number (weights by kind and by item group, stacks, limits, the
  slowdown math). Small hooks only: `Items.stack_size` asks it for the default stack, `Inventory.load_data` splits
  old saves' 100-stacks into free slots (never deletes; a full bag keeps the big stack), `Dwarf._update_carry` checks
  the load 5 times a second and multiplies the speed, overloaded blocks jump (dwarf.gd) and dodge (dwarf_fight.gd).
  HUD: "Weight 142 / 200" under the Bag title, yellow "Heavy" / red "OVERLOADED" inside the stamina bar's left end,
  and every item's hover text shows its weight.

  every PC, so each player's own dwarf works out its own slowdown. Nothing new to sync.

  two-step slowdown, satchel/perk/food bonus, old stacks split, and a live dwarf that is overloaded: slower, no jump,
  no dodge). `tests/test_inventory.gd` now reads the stone stack size instead of a fixed 100.
- **Hurdles (Claude's own):** (1) the design doc still said "No weight limit, only slots matter", so I replaced that
  line. (2) The owner picked "Deep Pockets +50", but the perk has 3 ranks, so I made it +25 per rank (+75 at full) and

## 2026-11-24 (PC) — Prow Hall rebuild no longer gets stuck (F819)
- **What we did:** found why the stone rebuild test stopped with "Waiting: something is in the way": 4 tower walls
  at 3.25 m (on the ring towers' odd sides) were never built, and the hall floors above waited for them.
- **The cause:** a ruin is placed all at once ("batch"). At the end of a batch the game only worked out how strong
  each piece is if something had been taken down. So every Prow Hall piece had strength 0. Normally that didn't show,
  because rebuilt pieces near the ground spread strength upwards. But these towers had nothing missing below 3.25 m,
  so no strength ever reached that wall, and a wall touching only "strength 0" pieces can't be built.
- **The fix:** `Builder.end_batch` now works the strength out once when pieces were added (nothing falls from it).
  New test `test_placed_ruin_has_its_strength` (no weak piece after placing, and the 4 walls can be built).
  Lesson written as RUIN-RULES 7.7.
- **Hurdles and mistakes:**
  1. My earlier offline copy of the rebuild said everything was fine, because it worked strength out piece by piece
     as it added them, unlike the game. Lesson: copy what the game really does, or print the real numbers in the game.
  2. The rebuild test takes about 35 minutes, so I wrote a 40-second probe that only places the ruin and prints the
     pieces round one stuck wall. All of them showed strength 0.00, which gave the answer.
  3. My first new test looked for the walls in the rebuild plan, which doesn't exist yet right after placing. I used
     the wall one storey up (same turn) instead.
  4. The full test run (54 min) showed a side effect of the Prow Hall's move to a natural cave (layout 19): one
     cave got 3 boulders. Two caves overlap there, and the shifted dice put a neighbour cave's boulder inside it. New
     worlds (layout 19) now skip a boulder spot that sits deeper inside another cave than its own; old worlds keep
     their boulders. `test_few_boulders_by_the_walls` passes again.
- **Full suite:** every Prow Hall test passes, including the 35-minute stone rebuild. Still failing, not ours: the
  sword-digs test (combat chats' unsaved work), the tower ground keep-clear test, robot saves, miner numbers, and one
  Jolt "too many bodies" error in the wood test.

## 2026-11-24 (PC) — No more slits between stacked walls (F833 🔁) and no 20 m Workbench rule (F837)

- **Problem (F833, came back from F165):** a wall, window or doorway standing on another one with no floor between
  them left a 25 cm open slit. Walls are 2 m tall, but a storey step is 2.25 m.
- **Three ways weighed:** (a) make walls stack 2.0 m apart. That would break the Prow Hall's 4.5 m storeys, and every
  ruin's plan would have to be made again. (c) Give every wall model a sill. That would shimmer against the
  floor's rim where there *is* a floor. (b) **Picked:** the game adds a beam by itself wherever a slit shows
  (`Builder.gap_fill_for`). Nothing is added where a floor's rim already fills the slit.
  Works for player building, every blueprint and every ruin, in any material.
- **Round 1:** a beam in the slit, refreshed whenever a nearby wall or floor is added or removed (`_refill_gaps`).
  New `tests/test_wall_gaps.gd` checks the Prow Hall (wooden + stonehold), every blueprint, and player stacking
  (wood, stone, mixed). New `buildcheck part=stacked` photo set.
- **Owner:** "still big gaps between the windows. Same with the walls." The wood wall's edges and the beam are
  *round* logs, so they only touch along a line, and a V-shaped crack stays see-through. The same crack shows
  between walls standing side by side.
- **Round 2:** the beam now reaches 6 cm into the wall below and the wall above (past the round logs). A thin dark
  lining goes at the back of every crack. Wood walls side by side also get an upright log over their seam
  (`Builder.seams_for`, one per pair, so nothing doubles up).
- **F837 (owner):** "remove the rule that we need a workbench within 20 meters to build". The distance check is
  gone. A Workbench must still exist somewhere, and its level still unlocks pieces. The message now says
  "Needs a Workbench (build one anywhere)".
- **Hurdles (Claude's own):**
  1. The first dark lining was 20 cm deep and painted black bands over the wall's own edge logs. Made it 4 cm, and
     the photo was clean.
  2. The build-menu test expected the whole new message, but the card cuts it at " (". Fixed the test.
  3. `git reset -q` after a commit reset the shared staging list. Other chats' staged files may have been unstaged.
     Next time, use only my own scratch index.
  4. `git add src/build/pieces.gd` swept in 2 lines from another chat that weren't committed yet (`yaw_of`
     FREE_ROT). They compile. The bag and food-slot chats say they aren't theirs, so they belong to a furniture
     chat that has finished. Lesson: stage only my own lines (`git add -p` or a patch), never a whole shared file.

## Nov 24, 2026 (PC): Dungeon 5, the Tomb of Hald Ironbrow (F843)

**What we did.** Built the fifth dungeon, all in the game with no 3D page first. It is a medium stone tomb (Stonehold `cut_stone`)
with 21 rooms on 2 levels. About half of its walls are broken, and 149 ceiling panels are gone so the dark rock shows through.
- **Ghosts only.** All 4 kinds, plus two new bosses:
  - **The Shield-Brother.** A big Bearded Shade with a front shield. He carries the Bronze Key.
  - **Hald Ironbrow.** The ghost lord's body and moves under a new name. He rises from his coffin.
- **Traps.** Each has a clue and a safe way through:
  - the dart-wall tripwires in the Hall of Candles and the Collapsed Tunnel
  - the loose stones over the Statue Corridor
  - the spike pit under the Broken Stair
  - the 10 m chasm under the Bridge of Oaths
  - the Embalmers' hidden boulder and spiked chest
- **The way out.** A Bronze door (it needs the Bronze Key) → the Grave Chamber's recipe stand → the secret stair → the lever behind the barred gate.
- **How it's made.** A Python script (`tools/dungeons/make_hald.py`) writes the whole plan. Decor and junk are placed with the shared helpers (`decor.py`, `junk.py`).
- **How to try it.** The start menu has "Dungeon 5, Tomb of Hald Ironbrow".
- **Tests.** A new test file, `tests/test_hald.gd`. It also proves the dart trap fires and the key drops.

**First, the lessons.** I read every journal note from dungeons #1-#4 and wrote the lessons into
`docs/design/zone1-dungeons/2026-11-24-hald-decisions.md`, so this dungeon wouldn't repeat them.

**Mistakes and hurdles**
- The script that reads the map also caught the `deadly = ["stair_pit", "chasm"]` line as if it were a room ("could not
  convert 'chasm'"). Fix: skip any match that has quotes in it.
- A bash heredoc holding Python with `r'''` broke ("unexpected EOF"). Fix: edit the file with the editor tool instead.
- Some wall decor touched torches or stood on the walking lines. Fix: moved them, and dropped the skeleton-with-note and
  the shield walls in the too-narrow Shield Hall.
- Junk placement crashed on the secret stair (`KeyError`), because stairs have no single floor height. Fix: a stair returns "no floor".
- I changed how often torches appear, and that broke the decor checks. Fix: went back to every 4th wall.
- The decor test counts stair pieces as doors (it wants 2 m clear), and an honour guard stood too close to one. Fix: moved it.
- The junk test thought the whole deep level (floor -8) was a drop, and some junk sat on stairs or at the pit's edge.
  Fixes:
  - The test knows Hald's deep floor is real floor.
  - A filter keeps junk off stairs and 0.8 m back from the pit and chasm.
  - "Level 2" now means below -5 m, so the stair pit counts as level 1.
- **The biggest catch.** Nothing in the game ever called "drop the boss's key" (`DungeonKeys.drop_key`). The Shield-Brother would have died
  without dropping the Bronze Key, and the last door would never open. Fix: any monster with a `key` drops it when it
  dies (`MonsterManager._kill`), and a test checks it. I also broke that test on purpose once, to be sure it really runs.
- Small test slips:
  - forgot to set the GODOT path in a new shell
  - GDScript couldn't tell the type of a filtered count
  - a key list came back as StringName, not String
- Not mine: `test_dungeon_list.test_each_dungeon_teaches_its_own_recipe` fails because of another chat's unfinished
  zone-1 loot changes (`recipe_of` now takes 2 values).
- Speed: the robot run showed only 10-37 frames a second inside the tomb (about 1,500 draw calls). Left for later.

**Left for later chats**
- The 3 new models (collapsing stairs, cracked bridge slabs, locked round stone door) and their traps.
- The Honour Chapel's portcullis ambush.
- The Shield-Brother's visible ghost shield.
- The fluffy moss in the broken parts.
- Making the tomb faster.

# Stairs: open preview, flush snapping, straight-on double stairs (F840, F839, F838), Nov 24

**What we did:**
- **F840:** the green stair preview was a solid stepped block down to the floor. Now it draws only the steps, open
  underneath like the built stair (`PieceMesh._open_steps`).
- **F839:** a stair aimed at another stair now snaps flush: aimed at its top end, it goes straight on (one stair up,
  one ahead); aimed at its side, it goes beside it at the same height (`Pieces.snap_stairs_on_stairs`). No side walls
  are added (owner's choice). Tests in `test_stairs_down`: snap straight on / beside / beside turned, and a robot dwarf
  walks up two flights and back down with no bump or stall.
- **F838:** where a storey is taller than one stair (Prow Hall 4.5 m floors, Stone/Wooden Outpost), the blueprints had
  a landing floor + pillars between two flights. Now the 2nd flight goes straight on, with a triangle wall on both sides
  and a wall under the top flight (the owner's own rebuild): `BlueprintLibrary._stacked_stairs`. Rebuilding an old ruin
  from a save takes the old landing and pillars down (`Builder._under_flight`). New test `test_stacked_stairs`, robot
  shot `buildcheck part=stairs`, ruin rule 1.13.

**Hurdles and mistakes:**
- `tools/run_tests.sh` failed: Godot isn't on this PC's PATH. Found the exe from the running processes and set `GODOT`
  to the WinGet path before each run.
- The Prow stairs came out 2.25 m apart instead of 2 m: the blueprint pass that removes the slab under a stair on a
  floor (F169) also lowered the first of a stacked pair. Fixed: a stair with a flight straight on above it keeps its slab.
- `test_stairs_free_block` (F811: free block at both ends of every flight) failed for the stacked pairs, because the top
  of the lower flight runs into the next flight, not onto floor. Fixed: an end that joins another flight is skipped (the
  far end is still checked).
- Other chats had unfinished lines in `builder.gd`; I committed only my own lines (a filtered patch into the index).
- **My mistake:** to commit only my own lines of `builder.gd` I made a zero-context patch (`git apply --unidiff-zero`).
  Both blocks landed one line too early (one cut a function's comment off, one split an `if` from its body), so the
  committed `builder.gd` didn't parse. The file on disk was fine, so only the saved copy was broken. Found it by running the test
  in a clean copy (git worktree). Fixed by writing the corrected file straight into the index. Lesson: after a partial
  commit, check the committed file parses (`git show HEAD:file`, or a worktree).
- The full suite showed 27 fails. Most were other chats' half-saved work (main.gd parse error mid-edit, Jolt body
  limit, Foreman attacks). Mine: the Prow Hall stair test wanted floor at both ends of every flight (now skips an end
  that joins the next flight), and the Outpost and Prow Hall ruin plans still had the old landings (re-made with
  `make_outpost_ruin.py` / `make_prow_hall_ruin.py`; a feast table moved 1 m away from the new stair foot).
- Also found: the F833 round 2 / F837 commit (2390458a) left its `builder.gd`, `piece_node.gd` and `structure.gd`
  lines unsaved, so the committed `builder.gd` points at `Pieces.WORKBENCH_RANGE`, which no longer exists. Asked the
  owner before touching another chat's work.

## Owner's sound picks put into the game (Nov 24)

**What we did:** Downloaded the 32 Freesound sounds the owner picked (all CC0, licence checked on each page), trimmed silence,
matched loudness (peak -3 dB), and saved them as `assets/sfx/<slot>_<n>.ogg`. `src/sfx.gd` loads `_0, _1, …` and picks one at random, so each slot now has only the new sounds.
- LOVE slots (new sounds only): hurt, death, eat, refill, pickup, dig_break, chop, beetle_hiss, craft.
- Slots with no LOVE yet got their MAYBE picks so they can be judged: step, swing, hit, hit_heavy, block, parry, thud, waterfall_trickle, open (menu).
- Removed `snail_slam` files (snail has no such hit; code still names it, it just stays silent) and `snail_spit` version 3.
- `cave_drip_0.ogg` saved but NOT wired (new slot: needs the owner's OK where it plays).
- Not changed (no picks yet): clink, dig_soft, close (menu), shell_clank, shell_clunk, build, beetle_rumble, plus the keepers.
- Ideas only, nothing built: 816051 for placing wooden pieces; 244985 for repairing; chop 177045 for making planks; parry 37596 for equipping the sword; cave_drip 341922 for small waterfalls.

**Mistakes / hurdles (mine):**
1. First script deleted the old sounds *before* encoding; this ffmpeg has no `libvorbis`, so every encode failed. Fixed: `git checkout -- assets/sfx` restored them, then I used ffmpeg's built-in `vorbis` encoder and only delete old files after all new ones are made.
2. `bc` printed ".2027" (no leading 0), which broke a fade setting. Fixed with printf.
3. Footstep 537835 was one long scrape, not clearly steps; I cut 0.5 s from it. Some clips are only ~0.3 s, so loudness-matching used peak level instead of LUFS.
4. The Freesound previews are 128 kbps mp3 (the site's best free preview), re-encoded to ogg, so tiny quality loss.
5. The old CREDITS.md rows for replaced sounds are still there; the new block says it replaces them.
- Hurt has a test needing 4 takes, so I added the MAYBE pick 257709 as the 4th.

  and a square chimney with a cap: the tower is now about 23 m tall (the cave must be about 24 m there),
- a thinner round top and a railed deck on the furnace house, plus a small porch with a sloped roof,

- a 6-sided watch turret on the terrace's front-right corner.

owner picked 6-sided turrets (3.5 m across) with ladders. The tower's corner turrets became stone spires instead.

  saving the script as a file first.

## 2026-11-25 (PC) — Tin ore in Zone 1's walls (F697, Zone 1 metal plan step 3)

- **Goal:** step 3 of `docs/decisions/2026-11-24-zone1-metal-and-loot.md`: tin ore as a new cave wall rock, so
  bronze (step 4) has its second ingredient. Claimed F697 in FEEDBACK.md first.
- **Followed copper's path:** copper is rock number 3 in `src/world/mat.gd`; the cave maker decides per 2 m block
  whether a wall spot is ore (`_is_ore`), the terrain shader paints it from baked texture slices, and the authority
  says which pickaxe is strong enough (`ore_too_hard`).
- **Built:**
  - `Mat.TIN = 6` (a free number): hardness 40, needs tier 1 (Copper Pickaxe), drops `tin_ore` (3 bits = 1 ore),
    6 mining XP. New `Mat.is_ore()` so tin also gets "always at least one ore" and the Ore Smasher perk.
  - `ore_too_hard`: stone pickaxe, Fang Pickaxe and bare hands bounce off tin with "Make a Copper Pickaxe at the Anvil".
  - Item `tin_ore` (grey, "Sn"): weight like ore, goes in ore crates and builders, a "where to get it" hint.
  - Cave maker: own noise (`_tin_noise`, seed + 404), only on the Mossy side, a little rare (the test keeps it between 0.2% and 3% of rock), never where
    copper is, never in the start room, and kept 4 m away from everything built (`reserved`: tower, Outpost and the
    other ruins, dungeon doorways and dungeons) and 7 m from a place's middle (camps, shrines, halls). Both the
    one-voxel path and the fast "all rock" path (`_fill_tin`) use it.
  - Look: `bake_terrain_looks.py` paints chunky lopsided grey-silver chips (5-7 sided, light worn rim, dark gap) on
    our 4 painted stone looks; the chips also go in the alpha channel, so the shader gives them a soft metal glint
    (dimmer than copper). Only tin's 4 slices changed (checked pixel by pixel against the old file).
  - Dropped-item model `tin_ore.glb` (Blender, same `ore()` builder as copper/silver, grey stone + dull chips);
    icon = the copper ore icon with its orange turned grey by script. CREDITS.md row added.
- **Tests:** `test_tin_in_mossy_walls` (rare but all around, none in the Jungle), `test_tin_needs_the_copper_pickaxe`,
  and the placement rule test `test_tin_keeps_out_of_built_places` (samples every built place on 3 seeds, and also
  builds the real rock blocks around each one with `generate_block`).
- **Hurdles:**
  1. Copper ore never checked built places at all (a helper found the `reserved` list). Tin checks it.
  2. First test run: tin still showed up at the edges of built places on 2 of 3 seeds. Cause: tin is decided per
     2 m block from the block's middle, so a block whose middle was just outside could still reach inside. Fix: a
     wider margin (4 m) and also looking 2.5 m below and 3 m above the middle.
  3. My own POI test sampled a 10 m cube (corners 8.7 m away) while the rule is 7 m; trimmed the test to 5.5 m.
  4. `run_tests.sh only=test_tin_...` ran nothing: `only=` takes the file name, `fn=` the test name.
  5. A Python script saving to a `/c/...` path failed on Windows: Python needs `C:/...` paths.
  6. CREDITS.md already had another chat's unsaved change: staged only my own line (built the file from HEAD + my
     row with `git hash-object` / `update-index`) so their work isn't committed by me.
- **Next:** step 4, the Bronze Ingot (1 Copper Ingot + 1 Tin Ore at the smelter) and the 13 bronze items.


## 2026-11-25: The Honour Chapel's portcullis ambush (F843, Tomb of Hald Ironbrow)

**What we did**
- New model `assets/models/dungeon/portcullis.glb`, built by `tools/asset_forge/builds/dungeon_portcullis.py`: the
  Stonehold round doorway itself ("frame") plus a rusted iron grille cut to the round hole ("gate"): an iron rim, 9
  square bars with spike teeth, straps riveted on both faces. Because the model *is* the doorway, it replaces the plain
  doorway at that junction, so there are never two stone frames in one spot (no shimmer). One render round was enough.
- `src/world/dungeon_build.gd`: a new "portcullis" kind. The host drops it when a living dwarf is 2.5 m into the
  Honour Chapel while the room's creatures live (MonsterManager.dungeon_room), and lifts it when they all die or when
  no living dwarf is left in the room. State in `world_state.dungeon_shut` + an rpc, like the hand doors, so friends
  who join see it the same. It slams down in 0.25 s with a heavy hit sound and grinds up in 2.5 s. Only the gate's own
  collision box comes and goes. It is unbreakable (added to both "can't hit this" lists).
- `tools/dungeons/make_hald.py`: the broken_stair -> honour_chapel doorway gets the portcullis; plan regenerated.
- Two new tests in `tests/test_hald.gd`: the ambush (raised at the start, half a step in = nothing, deeper = it
  slams, he dies = it lifts, everyone leaves = it lifts) and "every open stone doorway lets you through".

**Mistakes and hurdles**
- **Every Hald doorway was a solid wall (found while testing).** Models without their own collision boxes get one big
  box round the whole model. The Stonehold doorway (`build/doorway__cut_stone.glb`) had none, so each of Hald's
  doorways was blocked, hole and all. Hald is the first stone dungeon, so nobody had walked one yet. Fixed: it now gets
  side and top boxes like the plank doorway, and the new test walks every one.
- The "is it blocked" test first flagged the way-out gate, the round door and the Bronze door: those are *meant* to be
  shut. The test now skips doorways that have a real door in them.
- A "material is null" engine error appeared in my new test. It came from the Shield-Brother test before it, which frees
  its whole World at the end of the frame, and the error landed in whatever test ran next. Moving my tests above it
  (keeping that test last, with a note) fixed it. Making it free right away only moved the error into that test.
- A long Python edit sent through a bash heredoc broke on quoting (the RTK hook rewrites commands). Writing the script
  to a scratch file and running it worked.
- Another chat had uncommitted lines in `dungeon_build.gd` and `CREDITS.md` (footstep dust, tin ore), so only my own
  lines were committed, through a scratch git index.

**Also this session**
- The owner asked for food and level 15 every time Dev Dungeon starts: `src/debug/dungeon_test_start.gd` now gives 10 each
  of stew, miner's pie, beetle roast, moss ale and bellcap juice, and raises the dwarf to level 15 (with the 15 perk points).
  The owner's next screenshot still showed level 2: that run had started before the change, so a restart is needed.
- The owner's Tomb of Hald play test was logged as F846-F859, plus F860 🔁 (dungeons too bright, back for the 3rd time,
  so it went into "Things that keep coming back" with a different plan: dimmer and fewer lights, not more junk).
- Hurdle: main had moved on GitHub, and other chats had unsaved changes in CREDITS.md and main.gd, so pulling first
  would have mixed their work in. My commit went in through a scratch git index; the pull waits for a clean moment.


## Nov 25: three Tomb of Hald bugs from the owner's play test (F846, F847, F848)

**What we did**
- **F846, dying at full health before the boss room.** The spike pit under the Broken Stair has an "if you are down
  in here, you die" check. That check had a top (1.2 m over the pit's floor) but **no bottom**. The tomb door and the
  north edge of Hald's Tomb lie 5 m straight under the pit, so walking through them counted as "in the pit". Fix:
  the check now also needs you to be no more than 2 m under the pit's floor (`DungeonBuild.deadly_space`).
  The stairs over the pit were never the problem; the room under it was.
- **F847, invisible walls and platforms on the stairs.** Same cause as last chat's doorway bug: a dungeon model with
  no collision boxes of its own gets one big box round the whole model. Hald's 20 stone stairs had none, so each was a
  solid 2 m block: you stood on air on its top and bumped its sides. Fix: in a dungeon, every `stairs__*` piece now
  gets the same slanted slope the stairs you build get (`PieceNode.stairs_slope`).
- **F848, the boss room's door didn't open.** The Bronze door behind Hald's coffin opens with the Bronze Key. The lock
  code (`DungeonKeys.ask_unlock`) was written long ago, but **nothing ever called it**: E on the door did nothing.
  Hald is the first dungeon with a key door, so nobody had tried it. Fix: E on a key door now shows
  "Locked door (the Bronze Key) · E to unlock" and asks the host to unlock it.
- New tests in `tests/test_hald.gd`: `test_over_and_under_the_spike_pit_is_safe`, `test_walk_up_every_stair`,
  `test_the_bronze_door_opens_with_its_key` (the Shield-Brother test stays last).

**Mistakes and hurdles**
- The handoff guessed the pit's kill box reached *up* to the stairs. It reached *down* instead. Reading the map's
  numbers (the pit and the tomb door share the same x/z) found it.
- The handoff guessed the boss door "listens for the room being won". It doesn't: it is a key door, and the E button
  was never joined to it.
- My first stairs test failed 6 times: the test's "dwarf ball" at the very top of each flight touched the real wall
  beside the doorway at the top. Not a bug in the game; the check now stops 60 cm before the top.
- `git pull` was blocked by other chats' unsaved files (CREDITS.md, src/main.gd). Another chat also had unsaved lines
  in `dungeon_build.gd`, so I committed only my own lines (a patch of just my parts), never `git stash`.
- Still open: the owner said "the stairs outside the dungeons are broken too". Not found which stairs; asked the owner.

## Nov 25: F861 the slit between two rows of a wooden steep roof

**What we did**
- The owner sent a picture from inside a wooden steep roof: a long band of cave rock showing between two roof rows.
  The F865 fix (the real roof model shows again instead of the plain code shape) had made this older problem visible.
- Cause: `shack_v2.py` built the roofs with `K.Slope(..., top_v=0.33)`, so the panel climbed only (rise − 0.33) over
  its length: 1.5 m instead of 2 m on a steep piece. Each row ended about 40 cm lower than the next row started.
- Fix: the 6 Shack sloped roofs (steep, gentle, both corner kinds) now climb the full rise (top_v 0). The shingles run
  up to under the top log, and a hidden dark board under the high edge and the +x side covers the 1 cm cracks
  between rows and between neighbours. The shingles now reach about 25 cm above the piece's box at the top edge.
  That's on purpose: it's the start of the next row's space, and a straight roof line needs it.
- The steep inner corner now starts 16 cm up, so its `model_lift` is 0.2. The new check from F865 caught that it
  would have been thrown out.

**Mistakes and hurdles**
- F865 was called done without looking at two rows together. Fixing the model's fit made the gap between rows show.
  Lesson: after making a roof model show, look at a stacked roof (two rows) from inside before calling it done.

  works out the same spot from the world number (co-op ready), and the tick follows the host's learned list.
  It stands inside the doorway's clear circle, so nothing the world grows lands on it.
- 5 new tests in `tests/test_hald.gd` (the Shield-Brother test stays last). All 5 models pass the model checks.

**Mistakes and hurdles**
- **Cracked wall, round 1:** the hole looked boxy and the dark backing filled most of it, because the backing's hole was
  smaller than the ragged gap in the stones. Fix: no single backing, but strips that follow the hole row by row.
- **The strips then shimmered** (model check): neighbouring strips touched face to face, and their edges sat 1 mm from the
  stones' joints, so they showed through. Fix: each strip overlaps its neighbour with a different thickness, and the edges
  stay 3-4 cm away from the joints.
- **Small slips:** a push was rejected because another chat had pushed first (pulled and pushed again). I also looked for
  `kit_zone1.py` in the wrong folder (it is in `tools/asset_forge/builds/`).
- **The test runner** counts each test as one "check", so "1 checks" means the whole test passed, not that only one line
  ran.

## Nov 25: fair and fun ghost fights in the Tomb of Hald Ironbrow (F849, F850, F851, F872, F873, F874)

**What we did**
- **Teleports (F873):** a ghost that loses a quarter of its health used to jump to a random spot 3 to 5.5 m away,
  sometimes into a wall. Now it comes back right behind the dwarf who hit it (1.7 m; a bit to the side if a wall is
  in the way, never in front). A spot only counts if it's on your floor, has room all round the ghost's body, is
  inside the dungeon's rooms (not the spike pit or chasm) and has no wall between you and it. No good spot: no jump.
  When it shows again it swings an overhead "Ambush Chop" at once (the owner's F849 idea).
- **Ghosts standing idle (F873):** two causes. A ghost knocked down could never get up: its rig (the ghost body on
  the dwarf skeleton) has no animation player, and the shared knock-down/get-up code used one. And a jump never reset
  the "can't get closer" timer, so a ghost that came back further away sometimes gave up. Both fixed.
- **Parry star (F851):** ghosts never asked for the star: other creatures flash it on a hand bone, ghosts hold their
  mace in the dwarf rig's grip. Now every ghost swing flashes it on the mace head 0.4 s before the blow.
- **Doors and walking backwards (F872):** ghosts ran straight at you, so in the next room they pushed into the wall
  beside the doorway. Now in a dungeon they go room by room (the map's rooms that share a 1.2 m+ opening are linked,
  shortest way, never through the pit or chasm). They also look where they walk (before, only a chase turned them).
- **Shield-Brother (F850):** a ghostly bronze shield you can see; he turns slowly (step round him); his shield
  drops while he swings and just after; a Shield Charge when you keep away. The Honour Chapel grew from 8x8 to 10x12 m.
- **Hald (F849):** runs 4.3 (faster than walking), shorter rests, and two weak Tomb Shades (new kind `hald_shade`)
  rise with him.
- **Hit sound (F874):** `ghost_hit` (cloth whump, dull thump, breath of mist), made by `tools/art/make_ghost_hit.py`
  from our CC0 recordings.

**Mistakes and hurdles (Claude's own)**
- I first hung the parry-star timer on the mace grip as a Timer node. The dwarf's hand code takes the grip's last
  child for the weapon, so every ghost threw hundreds of errors. Fix: a scene-tree timer (nothing added to the grip).
- Then that timer's little function held the grip itself; when a test ended first, Godot complained the grip was
  freed. Fix: it holds a weak reference and checks it is still there.
- A typing slip (`var held := weakref(...)`) broke every script that uses the ghost rig ("Variant" warning counts as
  an error here). Found with `--check-only` on each script.
- My first "behind you" test failed: the test dwarf floats 1.5 m over the floor, and I compared the spot's floor with
  the dwarf's height. Now it compares with the floor under the dwarf (also right when you jump).
- One new test caught an error left over from the test before it (a freed model). Moved the new tests before the
  last old one, so the leftover error falls at the end again, as before.

**3rd round of the owner's play (same day)**
- Praise: "the parry right now is very satisfying with the sparks".
- **"I haven't seen a single teleport" (F873 🔁):** the real cause was my own body-room check. Its low test ball sat at
  0.6 m, and the tomb's floor tiles stand about 0.25 m over the rock, so the ball touched a tile at every spot and no
  spot ever passed. My test had used a plain cave without tiles, so it passed anyway. Now the balls sit at 0.95 and 1.45 m,
  and a new test builds the real tomb and finds a spot behind you in 3 of its rooms.
- **"They sometimes lie down" (picture):** a dazed ghost leaned far over. Now it only sinks 12 cm and bows a little.
- **"They go up a few stairs, then stop and go back" (F572 🔁):** three "give up" timers (the 15 s grudge, "can't get
  closer", "standing still for 3 s") ended the chase on the stairs. Now a ghost that saw you follows you anywhere in the
  dungeon, and only when you leave the dungeon does it vanish back to its spot, as the owner asked.
- **"He does two attacks and then just stands there" (F849 🔁):** every parry staggered Hald and cut his combo short,
  and the owner parries a lot. Now a parry still sparks and fills his daze bar, but his four blows all come unless the
  bar is full. The new test failed with the fix switched off and passed with it on.
- **Spiders (owner: "add lots of tiny spiders like in the 1st dungeon, but more"):** 16 Cave Spiders (Mossgate has 7)
  in 10 rooms, most up in the corners. One first landed on a bone pile, and the placement check caught it, so I moved it.
  The old "every creature is a ghost" test now allows spiders.
- Logged but not fixed: the secret stash hole is too big (F857 🔁, the Hald stone look chat's wall), and "trap still not
  fixed with a lever" (unclear which trap: asked the owner).
- Full suite: 986 checks, 5 tests failing, none from this work (pickaxe, roof models, ruin pages, an old Foreman check, a
  physics body limit).

**Tests:** test_ghost (4 new), test_hald (4 new; the Shield-Brother key test stays last). All pass.

## Nov 25: Ghosts can't be stunned, always swing after a teleport, and climb the Grand Stair (F873 🔁, F852, F897, F898)

**What the owner said (Tomb of Hald, 4th round):** sometimes a ghost teleports and then does nothing, maybe because it was hit too hard. Ghosts must never be stunned. After every teleport a ghost should be behind you, facing you, and attack. The blue ghost sometimes runs at you and does nothing. And ghosts you lure up the stairs get stuck on them.

**What we did:**
- **No stun for ghosts:** their stun bar is now so big it can never fill, and "fall apart" knockdowns skip ghosts. (We tried "infinity" first. A friend's copy of the game multiplies the bar by 0, and infinity × 0 is not a number, so we used a huge number instead.)
- **Always swing after a teleport:** when a ghost fades away, it forgets any daze and any push from your hit. It comes back in "chase" mode, facing you, and swings at once. Even if it was in the middle of something else as it faded, it switches back to chasing.
- **Blue ghost:** its only blow is a swooping lunge. No creature could start a lunge closer than 2 m, so right next to you it had nothing to do and just ran into you. Ghosts may now lunge from close up. The Lost Miner keeps the old rule (it circles and waits on purpose).
- **The Grand Stair:** a new test lets a ghost chase you from the Hall of Names to the top. It failed in three places, one after another:
  1. The stair slope is 45°, and creatures could only climb 45°. Ghosts can now climb 52°, like the dwarf.
  2. A "pit ahead?" check looks down just ahead of the creature. On the stair, that spot was already under the thin stone slab, so the check saw only the floor far below, called it a pit and stopped. Now it looks from as high as a stair rises over that distance.
  3. At the top, the hall floor's edge is a lip about a hand high. Round feet press against it like a wall. Ghosts now rise over low edges when there's room above them.

**Mistakes and hurdles (Claude's own):**
- I inserted a debug print into the wrong `move_and_slide()` in monster.gd and broke the file. Another Claude chat couldn't run any tests until I fixed it. They told me, and I removed it. Lesson: after adding a temporary line, run one test right away and look for "SCRIPT ERROR".
- I first thought the "may I step there?" room check was blocking the ghost. Printing each check separately showed it was the "pit ahead" check. I undid my room-check change because it wasn't needed.

**Tests:** test_ghost (2 new: hard hit never stuns + swings facing you; blue ghost swings when right next to you), test_hald (new: a ghost follows you up the Grand Stair), test_lampwick, test_monsters.

## Nov 25: Ghosts can't be pushed, a missed jump is made later, Hald walks round tombs (F901, F902, F873 4th time)

**What the owner said:** "Make sure I cannot knock away ghosts ... if I shoot them from far away, a lot of them stop
teleporting ... I hit them twice, they teleport, and my third combo just knocks them away when they're behind me.
For the boss, if I'm standing behind a tomb, he is trying to hit me through the tomb. He just needs to go around it."

**What we did**
- **No push (F901):** `Monster.knock()` now does nothing for a ghost. Every push in the game (hits, the finisher, the
  shield bash, the spear, traps) goes through that one spot, so one line covers all of them.
- **Owed jump (F873, 4th time):** a ghost jumps behind you after each quarter of its health. The spot behind you has
  to be open floor. If you stood in a narrow doorway or corridor (where you often shoot from), there was no open spot
  and that quarter's jump was simply lost. Now the ghost remembers it "owes" a jump and looks again 3 times a second
  while it chases you, until a spot opens up. It also tries two more spots, a little ahead of beside you.
- **Round the tomb (F902):** a ghost now looks 1.6 m ahead. If a tomb or pillar is in the way, it turns left or right
  (and sticks to that side, so it doesn't wobble in front of the tomb) until the way is open. It also won't start a
  swing if stone stands between it and you.
- Three new tests: no blow pushes a ghost; a jump it couldn't make is made later; it steps round a tomb and won't
  swing through it.

**Mistakes and hurdles**
- My first edit script stopped halfway: one piece of text it looked for had different tabs than I thought. The first
  two files were changed and the third wasn't. I checked which parts had landed before trying again.
- I wrote `for h in [0.7, 1.2]` without saying `h` is a number. Godot refused to load the whole ghost file, and for a
  minute that broke every test (other chats' too). Fixed by writing `for h: float in ...`. Lesson again: check that a
  file loads right after every edit.

## Same session: every creature's own death sound (F903) and real death traps in the Tomb of Hald (F904)

**What the owner said:** "Fix the enemy dying, it doesn't match anyone" (I asked: it was the sound) and "add a few
spikes and fake floor please, we don't have a full death trap anywhere" (they picked the Tomb of Hald, instant death).

**What we did**
- **Death sounds:** only bats and snails had their own (F881); everything else died with one dull thump. A new script
  (`tools/art/make_death_sounds.py`) mixes sounds already in the game (all from CC0 recordings) into four new ones:
  a beetle's shell cracking and a hiss running out, a spider's short hiss and curling legs, a skeleton falling into
  a heap of bones, and a ghost's slow breath sinking away. Ghosts and skeletons get theirs automatically (by the
  "ghost" and "rises" marks in the creature list), so new ones won't fall back to the thump. A test checks that no
  creature still uses it.
- **Death traps:** the tomb's plan had "the collapsing steps come next" and "the cracked slabs: next" written in it,
  but they were never made, so nothing there could kill you. Now four loose stone slabs give way the moment you stand on
  them: one over a new spike pit in the Hall of Candles, one over a new pit in the Hall of Names, and two cracked slabs
  on the Bridge of Oaths over the chasm (on opposite sides, so there's always a safe way across). They reuse Mossgate's
  breaking floor, but in stone with a stone crack sound (Hald is a stone tomb, F856).

**Mistakes and hurdles**
- The first rebuild of the tomb moved half the junk and ceiling holes, because the new traps used up the same dice as
  the rest of the tomb. I gave the traps their own dice, so everything else stays where it was.
- My new ghost tests passed alone but failed in the full run with "material is null". Cause: when a test cleaned up,
  the ghost's see-through paint was freed along with its body, and the dummy renderer's error showed up in the
  *next* test. The game already removes that paint first; now the test cleanup does too.
- Twice more I forgot to tell Godot a variable's type (`fakes := ...filter()`), and the test file didn't load. Fixed
  with `: Array`.

**What we did:** asked the owner how the play test of the Tomb of Hald went after the ghost fixes
(F901 no knock-back, F902 walk round tombs, F873 owed ghost jumps, F903 death sounds, F904 fake floor traps).
The owner said everything was good. F873 (ghosts not teleporting, said 4 times) had been waiting for the owner's
look, so it was moved out of "Things that keep coming back" in FEEDBACK.md and into FEEDBACK-done.md as confirmed.

**Mistakes and hurdles:** none this time. The 4th fix (keep the missed jump "owed" and retry it until there is room
behind the player) was the one that stuck. Lesson: when a fix keeps coming back, look for the case where the
action is skipped for good (here: a narrow doorway) instead of only making the normal case better.
